notes.7v.11: Some letters here are special manuscript characters that may not display (the numerals íí with a final accented j are iij, three): 'arka', 'erkr' and 'oꝛkum' are read as forms of mǫrk, 'mark'; 'bte' as bǿte, 'let [her] pay'; 'liis' as langlífis; 'ꝼtr' as fǿtr, 'feet'; 'haa' as hafa, 'have'. 'He' in 7v.11 is not named here, probably the bishop. Finns are the Sami, visited for soothsaying. 'Heathen' in 7v.18 means unbaptised; the practice is not explained. 'hor' (7v.23) is read as hǫrr, 'flax', since the same line spells hair 'har'; 'frauða fǿtr' as frogs' feet. 'til jafns réttar' (7v.1a-2a) is translated literally; its legal sense is unclear. 'dyð' (7v.8b) is uncertain. bókmál (7v.19a), 'book-speech', is taken as the written church law.

nodes.text: an *úbótamaðr* [a man beyond atonement]. Then he has a claim to three marks
of the property of the *úbótamaðr*, and the king
to all that is over and above. It is a deed beyond
atonement to make journeys to the Finns, to go to ask for
prophecy. If a woman bites a finger or
toe off her child for [its] long life,
let her pay three marks. And if a woman feeds a child
[while it is] heathen, or the husband [does], for long life, let [them] pay
three marks for it. She is the worst witch
who destroys a cow or a calf, a woman
or a child. And if witch-
craft is found in the beds or
bolsters of people, flax or frogs'
feet, human hair, nails, or those
things that seem likely [to serve] for spells,
then a charge may be brought against three women, with
equal right, those who seem likely
to be [guilty]. She must stand [the ordeal of] iron for it. If she proves
clean at the iron, then she is free of the charges.
If she proves foul at the iron, then she is declared
proven in the case; she has forfeited property and peace,
and has five days' truce from the iron; [after that she is] killable
and [may be] put to death wherever she can be caught. If a woman
is said in the district to practise *trylska* [troll-craft], then she shall
have six women as witnesses that she
is not *trylsk* [given to troll-craft]; [she is] free of the charge if she
gets that. But if she does not get them, let her go
away out of the district with her goods.
She herself is not to blame that she is
a troll. People shall believe well in God,
and not in curses or in heathen sacrifice.
But if a man is proved guilty of this, that
he deals in heathen sacrifices that are forbidden
by book-law, he is fined
three marks. On the separation of spouses.
